puzzles.opening: I went to the pantry in my hall. The fire alarm rang. What happened?
puzzles.answer: I cooked food with a very high temperature (without burning the food) in the pantry. However, I forgot to turn on the exhaust fan. Since the smoke detecter in the building is very sensitive, the grease fumes triggered the fire alarm.

puzzles.opening: After being mugged, a company president avoided carrying large sums of cash. An unavoidable situation made him put one million yen in a bag. Worried that criminals would attack if they discovered it contained one million yen, he added more cash. Why?
puzzles.answer:
His daughter had been kidnapped, and the kidnappers demanded fifty million yen in ransom.
To save money, he prepared bundles made mostly of blank paper, with genuine banknotes on the outside. The bag appeared to contain the full ransom, but the genuine money amounted to only one million yen.
He feared that the kidnappers would attack him if they discovered the deception. He therefore replaced the bundles at the top with bundles consisting entirely of genuine banknotes.
This increased the actual amount of money in the bag and made a superficial inspection less likely to reveal the fake bundles underneath.

rubric.full_credit: The bag is kidnapping ransom consisting mostly of paper disguised as banknotes.
rubric.half_credit: Ransom identified without disguised paper bundles

puzzles.opening: Over a smartphone, a daughter begs for a life to be spared and a kidnapper shouts: bring one hundred million yen alone by noon tomorrow, or this hostage dies; no police. Hearing the demand, her father decides the ransom should not be paid. Why?
puzzles.answer:
The father is the hostage. His wealthy daughter is free and receives the kidnapper’s phone call.
The father hears the kidnapper order his daughter to bring the ransom alone. He fears that, once she arrives with the money, the kidnapper will kill both of them to eliminate witnesses.
His daughter is his only family. To protect her, he tells her not to pay the ransom or come to the meeting, even though refusing puts his own life at risk.
The explanation concerns the father’s fear and decision; it does not establish that the kidnapper eventually kills either of them.

TS034 scoring clarification v5: Score only the submitted final, applying the existing half-credit and zero-credit conditions consistently. Where a submission correctly identifies that the father is the hostage and the daughter is free, credit C1 in full. If it says his daughter could be harmed but omits the fear of witness killing if she arrives, award C2 half credit; if it states refusal but omits the protective self-sacrifice, award C3 half credit. An additional unsupported assertion that he knows he will be killed regardless of payment does not by itself negate the separately stated danger to his daughter or the fact of refusal; it does not establish the actual eventual outcome. This unsupported central explanation does not earn credit for the missing witness motive or self-sacrifice and cannot count as a complete solution. If the submission explicitly denies a relevant credited fact, apply the zero-credit rule to that checkpoint. Do not merge facts across submissions.

puzzles.opening: In a newly settled village in Meiji-era Japan, a father finds a brown bear eating his only daughter in the forest. He shoots it and weeps over her remains. Knowing these wary bears rarely attack unfamiliar living humans, he nevertheless fears other villagers will also suffer having relatives eaten. Why?
puzzles.answer:
Several days earlier, an epidemic had killed his daughter and several other villagers.
The new settlement had no crematorium and could not spare enough fuel to cremate the dead, so the villagers buried the bodies in the forest.
The father visited his daughter’s grave every day. On this visit, he discovered that a bear had dug up her body and was eating her remains. He shot the bear.
He feared that other bears would also dig up the graves and eat the dead relatives of other villagers. His concern was about bears consuming buried bodies, rather than attacking living people.
